subject: health
unitTitle: Fueling, Movement, Sleep, and Recovery Without Diet Culture
essentialQuestion: How do I keep my body supplied for school, work, and activity across a real week?

prompts.prompt: Explain adequate fueling for growth, school load, and activity in your own words and give a valid example.
Use a cited source, diagram, model, or documented process to show understanding of hydration across a day.
Apply sleep need, sleep debt, and circadian timing in high school in a new fictional situation. Show the decision process or cite the evidence used.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, or unsafe choice involving recovery after effort, illness, or a heavy week; correct it and explain why.

Connect evaluating supplement, energy-product, and fitness-industry claims with body respect and resisting appearance-based health messaging. Explain how the two support, constrain, or build on one another.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Evaluate three fictional wellness plans for adequacy, safety, evidence, flexibility, and cost, then revise the weakest one. No calorie counts, weights, body-size targets, diet rules, or good/bad food labels are used or produced.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy, and one next question.

adaptationChoices: Evaluation may be written, spoken, chart-based, or completed against a supplied criteria checklist. Learners with food allergies, medical diets, cultural or religious food practices, or limited food access work entirely with the fictional plans and are never asked to describe their own eating.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. No assessment requires disclosure, a recording, or any body measurement.
trustedAdultNote: Direct any urgent safety, health, or mental-health concern to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
